mainTopic: Which offerings need נסכים: the extra words in the פסוקים of libations and what each one includes
overview: The גמרא works through a ברייתא that uses extra words in the פסוקים about נסכים to show which offerings need libations. First it explains why the מצורע's חטאת and אשם each need their own source: they serve different purposes. It also proves that the word זבח means the מצורע's חטאת and not the נזיר's offerings, because only offerings that can come as a נדר or נדבה need נסכים. Next it asks why עולה means the מצורע's עולה and not the יולדת's. אביי says the יולדת is learned from the end of the פסוק, as רבי נתן teaches. רבא says three inclusions must point to the מצורע. רב ששת then explains that 'לאיל' includes the ram of אהרן, and 'או' includes the פלגס. The פלגס teaching fits רבי יוחנן but remains a difficulty for בר פדא. Finally, the summary פסוק teaches that only male sheep get different נסכים by age, and the amud ends as רב פפא begins telling how רבא tested his students.

steps.title: One word can cover both חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a נזיר where the single word זבח includes both a חטאת and an אשם. So why does our ברייתא need a separate word for the מצורע's אשם?
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: From where do we know that a sin offering and a guilt offering are included? The verse says "the sacrifice."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question with a source. In the case of a נזיר, the one word זבח already covers both a חטאת and an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא learned the מצורע's חטאת from זבח, and his אשם from a different word. But this other ברייתא shows that זבח alone can include both offerings. So the extra word for the אשם seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Guilt offering
"Sacrifice"; the word in the פסוק being expounded
"The verse teaches"; introduces a source from a פסוק

phrases.english: As the Master said:
From where do we know a sin offering and a guilt offering?
phrases.notes: This is about a נזיר who puts his shaved hair under the fire of his חטאת or אשם instead of under his שלמים (במדבר 6:18).

phrases.english: The verse says: "the sacrifice."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question from before this text: why the ברייתא needs a separate source for the מצורע's אשם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of a separate word to include the מצורע's אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא shows that the single word זבח includes both חטאת and אשם, so the extra source looks unnecessary.

steps.title: Same purpose needs one source, different purposes need two
steps.stepSummary: One word covers both offerings only when they serve the same purpose. For a מצורע, the אשם makes him fit and the חטאת atones, so two sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where both offerings are alike. But where the guilt offering is to make him fit and the sin offering is to atone, we need two verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It explains why the נזיר and the מצורע are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נזיר, the חטאת and the אשם play the same kind of role, so one word can include both. For a מצורע, the אשם makes him fit to return, while the חטאת brings atonement. Because their jobs are different, each one needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: "These words apply"; limits a rule to certain cases
Like each other; alike
To make fit (to return to normal status)
To atone
Two verses, meaning two separate sources

steps.whatToRemember: One word can cover two offerings only if they share the same purpose. The מצורע's אשם makes him fit and his חטאת atones, so each needs its own source.

phrases.english: This applies only where
the two of them are alike,
phrases.notes: He means the נזיר's offerings, which serve the same kind of purpose.

phrases.english: but where the guilt offering is to make him fit
and the sin offering is to atone,
we need two verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the purpose of the offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since זבח covers both offerings for a נזיר, it should cover both for a מצורע too.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source works only for offerings with the same purpose. The מצורע's offerings have different purposes, so they need two sources.

steps.title: Maybe זבח means the נזיר's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why זבח should refer to the מצורע's חטאת. Maybe it refers to the חטאת and אשם of a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The sacrifice": this is the sin offering of a leper. But say instead that it is the sin offering and guilt offering of a nazirite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's reading of the word זבח. Then it suggests a different way to read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says זבח teaches that the מצורע's חטאת needs נסכים. The גמרא suggests it might instead teach this about the נזיר's חטאת and אשם. If so, there would be no source for the מצורע's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת (a skin affliction) who brings offerings when he is purified
A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and impurity from the dead
"But say instead"; introduces another possible reading

phrases.english: "The sacrifice": this is the sin offering of a leper.
But say instead it is the sin offering and guilt offering of a nazirite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that זבח refers to the מצורע's חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the word itself points to the מצורע. It could just as well refer to the נזיר's חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: The נזיר's נסכים come only with his עולה and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. A ברייתא teaches that "their meal offering and their libations" for a נזיר refers only to his עולה and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That should not enter your mind, as it is taught: "And their meal offering and their libations": the verse is speaking about his burnt offering and his peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question from step 3. It proves from a ברייתא that the נזיר's חטאת and אשם do not get נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the נזיר's מנחה and נסכים is limited to his עולה and שלמים. So the word זבח cannot be teaching that his חטאת and אשם need נסכים. That leaves the מצורע's חטאת as what זבח refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: "It should not enter your mind"; rejects a suggestion
Libations (wine poured with an offering)
Burnt offering
Peace offering

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר's נסכים come only with his עולה and שלמים. So זבח must refer to the מצורע's חטאת.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as it is taught: "And their meal offering and their libations":
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:15, about the נזיר's offerings at the end of his term.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about his burnt offering and his peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 3 using a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the suggestion using a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זבח might teach that the נזיר's חטאת and אשם need נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר's נסכים go only with his עולה and שלמים, so זבח refers to the מצורע's חטאת.

steps.title: The ברייתא proves from a פסוק that the נזיר's נסכים go only with his עולה and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the נזיר's נסכים might also go with his חטאת. It answers by quoting the פסוק about the איל brought as a שלמים, together with its מנחה and נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the נסכים go with his עולה and his שלמים, or maybe even with a חטאת? The פסוק teaches: "And he shall make the ram a peace offering… and its meal offering and its libation."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from step 4. Here the ברייתא shows its source: the נזיר's נסכים go only with his עולה and שלמים, not with a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said that "their מנחה and their נסכים" means only the עולה and שלמים. This step brings the support for that claim: the פסוק ties the מנחה and נסכים to the איל, which is a שלמים. How that פסוק excludes the חטאת is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
His burnt offering
His peace offering
Its libation (the wine poured with an offering)

phrases.english: Do you say it refers to his burnt offering and his peace offering,
or perhaps it means even a sin offering?
phrases.notes: This means the חטאת a נזיר brings when he becomes טמא.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he shall make the ram a sacrifice of a peace offering
and its meal offering and its libation."
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:16–17

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּעוֹלָתוֹ וּבִשְׁלָמָיו, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ חַטָּאת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 4 and gives the source for its claim.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the נזיר's מנחה and נסכים belong only to his עולה and שלמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 6:17: the איל of שלמים with its מנחה and נסכים

steps.title: The ram is singled out so other offerings can be compared to it
steps.stepSummary: The איל already belonged to the general group of שלמים. It is mentioned separately so that other offerings can be compared to it: only offerings that can come as a נדר or נדבה need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ram was already included in the general rule. So why was it mentioned on its own? To compare other offerings to it. Just as a ram is special in that it can come as a נדר or נדבה, so too any offering that can come as a נדר or נדבה needs נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the פסוק about the איל excludes the חטאת. It uses a היקש: offerings are compared to the איל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All שלמים already need נסכים, so naming the איל separately must teach something new. The lesson is that only offerings like the איל need נסכים, meaning offerings that can be brought as a נדר or נדבה. A חטאת or אשם is never brought that way, so the נזיר's חטאת and אשם need no נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: It was already included in the general rule
So why was it singled out?
To compare (to make a הֶקֵּשׁ)
A vow offering: "I take upon myself to bring an offering"
A gift offering: "This animal is an offering"

steps.whatToRemember: Only offerings that can come as a נדר or נדבה need נסכים. That is why the חטאת and אשם have none.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule (נדר or נדבה) decides which offerings need נסכים. It explains why the נזיר's חטאת and אשם have none.

phrases.english: The ram was already included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: All שלמים need נסכים, and the איל is a שלמים.

phrases.english: so why was it singled out?
In order to compare others to it.
Just as a ram is special
in that it can come as a vow or a gift offering,
so too, anything that can come as a vow or a gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיִל בַּכְּלָל הָיָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָא? לְהַקִּישׁ אֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 5 excludes the חטאת.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the נזיר's חטאת and אשם need no נסכים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A היקש to the איל, which can come as a נדר or נדבה

steps.title: Why say עולה means the מצורע's burnt offering and not a יולדת's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges another reading in the first ברייתא. That ברייתא said the word עולה means the עולה of a מצורע. Maybe it means the עולה of a יולדת instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Burnt offering": this is the burnt offering of a מצורע. But why not say it is the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first ברייתא and questions how it reads the word עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the extra word עולה to include the מצורע's עולה in the need for נסכים. The גמרא asks why this word should not include the יולדת's עולה instead. If it did, the מצורע's עולה would have no source for needing נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering of a מצורע (one healed of צרעת)
The burnt offering of a woman who gave birth
But say instead… (proposes another reading)

phrases.english: "Burnt offering": this is the burnt offering of a leper,
but say it is the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עֹלָה״ – זוֹ עוֹלַת מְצוֹרָע, וְאֵימָא זוֹ עוֹלַת יוֹלֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חטאת question and challenges a different reading in the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that עולה means עולת מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word עולה could just as easily mean the יולדת's עולה. Then the מצורע's עולה would have no source.

steps.title: אביי: the יולדת's burnt offering is learned from the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the יולדת's עולה is already learned from the end of the פסוק. So the word עולה is left free to include the מצורע's עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The burnt offering of a woman who gave birth is learned from the end of the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 7. The יולדת already has her own source, so עולה must mean the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge works only if the יולדת's עולה needs the word עולה as its source. אביי shows she is already covered by the end of the same פסוק. So the word עולה has nothing to add for her and is used for the מצורע's עולה, just as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the פסוק
It is derived (learned from a source)

steps.whatToRemember: Each extra word must teach something new. The יולדת already has her source at the end of the פסוק, so עולה teaches the מצורע's עולה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The burnt offering of a woman who gave birth
is derived from the end of the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: עוֹלַת יוֹלֶדֶת מִסֵּיפָא דִּקְרָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the other case already has its own source, so the word is free for this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word עולה might be needed for the יולדת's עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יולדת's עולה is learned from the end of the פסוק, so עולה includes the מצורע's עולה.

steps.title: רבי נתן's source: 'for the lamb' is the יולדת and 'the one' is the eleventh animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports אביי. רבי נתן reads 'לכבש' as the יולדת's עולה and 'האחד' as the eleventh animal of מעשר, which is brought as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says, 'For the lamb' means the עולה of a יולדת. 'The one' means the eleventh animal of מעשר, which is brought as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what אביי just said. The end of the פסוק really is the source for the יולדת's עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the יולדת's עולה comes from the end of the פסוק. רבי נתן's ברייתא shows this clearly, because he reads 'לכבש' as the יולדת. He also reads 'האחד' as one more case: the eleventh animal of מעשר, which also needs נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering brought by a woman after giving birth
Here, the animal tithe: every tenth animal is made holy
The eleventh animal, wrongly called 'tenth' while counting, which becomes a שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: The eleventh animal is not the מעשר itself. It is the animal counted by mistake after the tenth, and it is brought as a שלמים.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Natan says:
"For the lamb" – this is the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:5

phrases.english: "The one" – this is the eleventh animal of the tithe
which is offered as a peace offering.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support אביי's answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the end of the פסוק teaches the יולדת's עולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי נתן reading 'לכבש' as עולת יולדת

steps.title: Why the eleventh animal needs its own source
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why a פסוק is needed for the eleventh animal. Without it we would think the secondary animal cannot be stricter than the main one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A source is needed, because nowhere in the whole Torah do we find that the secondary thing is stricter than the main thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the eleventh animal needs a special word in the פסוק to require נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real מעשר animal does not need נסכים. The eleventh animal only became holy because it was attached to the מעשר. So we would have thought it cannot have a stricter law than the מעשר, and the פסוק must teach that it does need נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary, attached to something else
The main thing
Stricter

phrases.english: For we have not found such a thing in the entire Torah,
that the secondary should be stricter than the main.
phrases.notes: The 'main' is the tenth animal, the real מעשר, which brings no נסכים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and explains why 'האחד' is needed for the eleventh animal.
steps.raayaObject: The need for a separate word to include the eleventh animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle that a טפל is never stricter than the עיקר

steps.title: רבא: three inclusions point to the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question of step 7 in a different way. Three inclusions in the פסוק must match a case with three offerings, and that is the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Which case needs three inclusions? You must say it is the מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to why the word עולה means the מצורע and not the יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי answered by showing that the יולדת is already learned from somewhere else. רבא instead points out that the פסוק has three inclusions, and the case that fits is the מצורע, who brings three offerings. So the inclusions all point to the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: Inclusions, extra words that add more cases
'You must say', meaning only one answer fits
A person with צרעת, who brings three offerings when he becomes pure

phrases.english: Rava says:
Which matter needs three inclusions?
phrases.notes: He means the three extra words in the פסוק, each adding one offering.

phrases.english: You must say: this is the leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה רִבּוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 7, next to אביי's answer in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word עולה could mean the יולדת's עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three inclusions match the מצורע's three offerings, so they refer to the מצורע.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'for the ram'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs the words 'לאיל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the ram': why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new question about another word in the פסוק on נסכים. It is setting up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amounts for a ram's נסכים are already written in another place. So the extra word 'לאיל' seems unneeded, and the גמרא asks what it comes to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For the ram'
'Why do I need it?' Asks what an extra word teaches

phrases.english: "For a ram" – why do I need it?
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about another word in the פסוק of נסכים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'לאיל' comes to include

steps.title: רב ששת: to include the ram of אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that 'לאיל' includes the ram of אהרן, the כהן גדול's ram, in the need for נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It comes to include the ram of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question: the word 'לאיל' adds the ram of אהרן to the list of offerings that need נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram of אהרן is the כהן גדול's ram, which is brought as an עולה on יום כיפור. We might have thought it is a special case without נסכים. The extra word teaches that it needs them like any other ram.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
The ram of אהרן, the כהן גדול's עולה on יום כיפור

steps.whatToRemember: Extra words in the פסוק of נסכים add cases: the יולדת, the eleventh animal of מעשר, the מצורע, and the ram of אהרן.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says:
To include the ram of Aaron.
phrases.notes: This is the ram the כהן גדול brings as an עולה on יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְרַבּוֹת אֵילוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאיל' includes the ram of אהרן in the need for נסכים.

steps.title: The ram of אהרן is already covered by 'on your festivals'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: the ram of אהרן should already need נסכים from the word 'במועדיכם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ram of אהרן is already learned from 'on your festivals'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer from step 13. It says we do not need 'לאיל' for the ram of אהרן, because another word already covers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from 'במועדיכם' that all required holiday offerings need נסכים. The ram of אהרן is brought on a holiday, יום הכיפורים, so it should already be included. That would make 'לאיל' extra for this purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram of אהרן; the ram the כהן גדול brings on יום הכיפורים
'On your festivals', a word in the פסוק that teaches holiday offerings need נסכים
It comes out from; it is learned from
The flour, oil and wine brought along with certain offerings

phrases.english: The ram of Aharon,
is learned from 'on your festivals'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's reading of 'לאיל' in step 13 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that 'לאיל' is needed to include the ram of אהרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'במועדיכם' already includes all required holiday offerings, and the ram of אהרן is one of them, so 'לאיל' would teach nothing new.

steps.title: We might have limited 'on your festivals' to communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without 'לאיל' we might think 'במועדיכם' only covers offerings of the צבור, not an individual's offering like אהרן's ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: that rule is only for communal offerings, but not for an individual's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It explains that 'לאיל' is still needed, because 'במועדיכם' might only cover offerings brought for the whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram of אהרן is brought by one person, the כהן גדול, so it is a קרבן יחיד. Holiday offerings in 'במועדיכם' are usually offerings of the צבור. So 'לאיל' is needed to show that this individual holiday offering also needs נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought; it would enter your mind to say
This rule applies only to...
The community; offerings brought on behalf of all of ישראל
An individual; an offering brought by one person

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
this applies only to offerings of the community,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule from 'במועדיכם' that holiday offerings need נסכים.

phrases.english: but to those of an individual – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּצִבּוּר, אֲבָל דְּיָחִיד – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the competing source, so the second source is still needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'במועדיכם' covers only communal holiday offerings, so the ram of אהרן, an individual's offering, would not need נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לאיל' teaches that the ram of אהרן needs נסכים even though it is an individual's offering.

steps.title: Why not learn from the יולדת's עולה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we would ever think an individual's offering does not need נסכים, since the יולדת's עולה is an individual's offering and needs them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is it different from the עולה of a woman who gave birth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 15. We already know from the יולדת's עולה (step 9) that an individual's offering needs נסכים, so why would we think otherwise?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said we might exclude an individual's offering. But the ברייתא in step 9 read 'לכבש' as the יולדת's עולה, which is brought by one woman and still needs נסכים. So the worry of step 15 seems already solved.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Why should this case be treated differently?
The burnt offering brought by a woman after giving birth
An offering brought by one person

phrases.english: And how is it different from the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth?
phrases.notes: Back in step 9, the ברייתא taught that this offering needs נסכים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that we might have excluded an individual's offering from needing נסכים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יולדת's עולה is an individual's offering that needs נסכים, so we already know individual offerings are included.

steps.title: An offering with a set time might be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the יולדת's עולה has no set time, while אהרן's ram does, so we could not learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: that rule is only for an offering with no set time, but an offering with a set time might not need נסכים. So the פסוק teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16. The יולדת's offering cannot teach about אהרן's ram, because one has a set time and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יולדת's עולה can be brought whenever she is ready, but אהרן's ram has a fixed day. We might have thought a fixed-time individual offering does not need נסכים. So 'לאיל' is truly needed, and רב ששת's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that has a fixed time when it must be brought
Something that has no fixed time
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: 'לאיל' includes אהרן's ram because no other source covers it: 'במועדיכם' might mean only communal offerings, and the יולדת's עולה has no set time.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי – דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן,
phrases.english: this applies only to something that has no fixed time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּבָר שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן – אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: but something that has a fixed time – I would say no.
phrases.notes: The ram of אהרן is brought on יום הכיפורים, so it has a set day.

phrases.english: So it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי – דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and settles רב ששת's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between the two cases (fixed time versus no fixed time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An individual's offering needs נסכים only when it has no set time, like the יולדת's עולה. A fixed-time individual offering, like אהרן's ram, would not.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לאיל' is needed to teach that אהרן's ram, a fixed-time individual offering, still needs נסכים.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'or for a ram'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra word 'או' in 'או לאיל' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'or for a ram'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next word in the פסוק. It asks why the word 'או', 'or', is written before 'לאיל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לאיל' was just explained, so now the focus is on the extra 'או'. The גמרא assumes every extra word in the פסוק teaches something new about נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking what an extra word teaches)
'Or for a ram', words from the פסוק about נסכים
A ram; a grown male sheep

phrases.english: 'Or for a ram' – why do I need it?
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:6. The question is really about the extra word 'or'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues expounding the same פסוק, now on the word 'או'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'או' before 'לאיל' comes to include.

steps.title: 'Or' includes the פלגס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'או' includes the פלגס, a sheep in between a lamb and a ram, in the need for נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include the פלגס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 18. The word 'או' teaches that a פלגס also needs נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives one amount of נסכים for a כבש (young sheep) and another for an איל (ram). A פלגס is in its thirteenth month, too old to be a lamb and too young to be a ram. Without 'או' we would not know it needs נסכים at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to add a case to the rule
A sheep in its thirteenth month, in between a lamb and a ram
A lamb; a sheep in its first year

steps.whatToRemember: The extra 'או' in 'או לאיל' includes the פלגס, a sheep that is neither a lamb nor a ram, in the need for נסכים.

phrases.english: To include the palges.
phrases.notes: A פלגס is a sheep in its thirteenth month: past being a lamb, not yet a ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'או' includes the פלגס, which the תורה never names, in the requirement to bring נסכים.

steps.title: The teaching about the פלגס fits רבי יוחנן but not בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the teaching from step 19. It fits רבי יוחנן, who holds a פלגס is its own creature, but not בר פדא, who holds it is only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for רבי יוחנן. He holds a פלגס is a separate kind of animal, as the משנה says: someone who brings a פלגס brings ram-נסכים with it, but it does not count as his required offering. רבי יוחנן said 'או לאיל' includes the פלגס. But what about בר פדא? He says the person brings ram-נסכים and makes a condition, because a פלגס is a doubt. Why would we need a פסוק to include a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the teaching 'או includes the פלגס' fits רבי יוחנן's view. Then it attacks that teaching according to בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, a פלגס is neither a lamb nor a ram, so it needs its own פסוק to require נסכים. According to בר פדא, a פלגס is really either a lamb or a ram, and we just don't know which. If so, it is already covered by the פסוק about lambs or the פסוק about rams, so an extra word to include it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion). It sets up a 'but for the other opinion' challenge.
It is its own creature, a category of its own
The wine, flour and oil offerings that go with a ram
He brings and stipulates, meaning he brings with a condition
A doubt, an uncertain case
To include

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and בר פדא agree that the person brings ram-sized נסכים. They argue about why. For רבי יוחנן, a פלגס is a separate category that the פסוק specifically includes. For בר פדא, the person brings the larger amount only to cover the doubt.

phrases.english: This works out well for Rabbi Yochanan,
who said it is its own creature,
phrases.notes: "It" is the פלגס from step 19, the sheep that is in between a lamb and a ram.

phrases.english: as we learned: if he offered it,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פרה 1:3, about someone who brought a פלגס.

phrases.english: he brings with it the libations of a ram,
but it does not count for him as his offering,
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Or for a ram" comes to include the palges.
But according to bar Padda, who said:
he brings them and makes a condition,
phrases.notes: He brings ram-sized נסכים and says: if it's a ram, all of this is for it; if it's a lamb, the extra is a donation.

phrases.english: because it is a doubt,
is a verse needed to include a doubtful case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 19 that 'או' includes the פלגס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching from step 19 that 'או לאיל' includes the פלגס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to בר פדא, a פלגס is really a lamb or a ram, so it is already covered and does not need its own word in the פסוק.

steps.title: The difficulty stands according to בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that, according to בר פדא, the challenge has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Certainly, according to בר פדא, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on answering for בר פדא. It openly says the question stays unanswered on his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered. The teaching that 'או' includes the פלגס works only for רבי יוחנן. For בר פדא, the extra word remains unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly it is difficult. The גמרא admits there is no answer.

steps.whatToRemember: The teaching that 'או לאיל' includes the פלגס fits רבי יוחנן, who holds a פלגס is its own creature. According to בר פדא, the גמרא leaves it as an unanswered difficulty.

phrases.english: Certainly, according to bar Padda, it is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that the challenge in step 20 cannot be answered for בר פדא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against בר פדא stands. The derivation of the פלגס from 'או' fits only רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'for the one bull'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a summary פסוק about נסכים and asks why the words 'לשור האחד' are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So shall it be done for the one bull, or for the one ram, or for the young of the sheep or the goats.' Why does the פסוק need to say 'for the one bull'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a פסוק that seems to just repeat earlier rules and asks what the words 'for the one bull' add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוקים already gave the amounts of נסכים for each animal. So this summary פסוק looks extra, and the גמרא wants to know what new rule the words about the bull teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? What does it teach?
So shall it be done

phrases.english: "So shall it be done for the one bull,
or for the one ram,
or for the young of the sheep or of the goats."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:11

phrases.english: "For the one bull": why does the verse need to say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about a different phrase in the same section on נסכים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new rule the words 'לשור האחד' teach.

steps.title: A bull and a calf get the same נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The words teach that, unlike a ram and a lamb, a grown bull and a young calf get the same amount of נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה gave different נסכים for a ram and a lamb. So we might think we should also give different נסכים for a bull and a calf. That is why the פסוק says 'for the one bull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22. The words 'for the one bull' tell us that all cattle, young or old, get one set of נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With sheep, age matters: a ram gets more נסכים than a lamb. Based on that, we might have split cattle by age too, giving a calf less than a bull. The word 'האחד' teaches that cattle have one rule for every age.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
A bull, a grown animal in its second year
A calf, a young animal in its first year
A lamb, a young sheep

steps.whatToRemember: A ram and a lamb get different נסכים, but a bull and a calf get the same נסכים. This is learned from 'לשור האחד'.

phrases.english: Since we have found that the verse made a difference
between the libations of a ram and the libations of a lamb,
one might think we should also make a difference
between the libations of a bull and the libations of a calf.
So the verse says: "for the one bull."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לשור האחד' teaches that bulls and calves share one rule of נסכים, unlike rams and lambs.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'or for the one ram'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the words 'או לאיל' in the summary פסוק are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or for the ram.' Why does the פסוק need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the same summary פסוק and asks what the words 'או לאיל' come to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amounts of נסכים for an איל were already given earlier in the פרשה. So the words seem to repeat what we already know. The גמרא assumes that every word in the תורה must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? (What does it come to teach?)
A ram, a male sheep in its second year or older

phrases.english: "Or for the ram"
phrases.notes: This is the next phrase in the same summary פסוק, במדבר 15:11.

phrases.english: why does the verse need to say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 22, now applied to the next phrase of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra teaching comes from the words 'או לאיל האחד'?

steps.title: All rams get the same נסכים, whatever their age
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה separated a one-year-old lamb from a two-year-old ram, we might split two-year-old rams from three-year-old rams. The פסוק says 'האחד' to teach that all rams are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we found that the פסוק made a difference between the נסכים of a one-year-old and the נסכים of a two-year-old, maybe we should also make a difference between the נסכים of a two-year-old and those of a three-year-old? So the פסוק says 'or for the one ram'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'האחד' teaches that every איל gets the same נסכים, no matter how old it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because age changed the amount once (כבש compared to איל), we might have thought that each extra year changes the amount again. 'האחד', meaning 'the one', tells us that there is one rule for all rams. Age stops mattering once the animal is an איל.

keyTerms.meaning: That the פסוק made a difference (gave different laws)
The נסכים (flour, oil and wine) that go along with a קרבן
One might have thought

phrases.english: Since we found that the verse made a difference

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין נִסְכֵי בֶּן שָׁנָה לְנִסְכֵי בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: between the libations of a one-year-old and the libations of a two-year-old,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל נְחַלֵּק בֵּין נִסְכֵי בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם
phrases.english: one might think we should make a difference between the libations of a two-year-old
and the libations of a three-year-old?
Therefore the verse says: "Or for the one ram."

steps.whatToRemember: Once an animal counts as an איל, its age no longer changes the amount of נסכים.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'האחד' teaches one amount of נסכים for every איל, whether it is two years old or three.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'or for the lamb among the sheep'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the words 'או לשה בכבשים' are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or for the lamb among the sheep.' Why does the פסוק need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next phrase of the פסוק and asks the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amounts for a כבש were already given, so this phrase also looks like a repeat. The גמרא looks for its extra teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A young animal from the flock
Lambs, young sheep

phrases.english: "Or for the lamb among the sheep"
why does the verse need to say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question, applied to the next phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra teaching comes from 'או לשה בכבשים'?

steps.title: Female sheep get the same נסכים whether young or old
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה separated a male כבש from an איל, we might also split a young female (כבשה) from an older female (רחלה). The phrase teaches that they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we found that the פסוק made a difference between the נסכים of a male lamb and the נסכים of a ram, maybe we should also make a difference between the נסכים of a female lamb and those of a grown ewe? So the פסוק says 'or for the lamb among the sheep'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this phrase teaches that a young female sheep and an older female sheep get the same נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With male sheep, age matters: a כבש and an איל get different amounts. We might have thought female sheep work the same way. The phrase teaches that for females there is no such split, and both get the smaller amount of a כבש.

keyTerms.meaning: A young female lamb
A grown female sheep, a ewe
A young male lamb (in its first year)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that a grown רחלה is treated like an איל. Only male sheep become an איל with bigger נסכים. Females of any age stay at the amount for a כבש.

phrases.english: Since we found that the verse made a difference
between the libations of a male lamb and the libations of a ram,
one might think we should make a difference between the libations of a female lamb
and the libations of a ewe?
Therefore the verse says: "Or for the lamb among the sheep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A young female lamb and a grown ewe get the same נסכים.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'or among the goats'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the words 'או בעזים' are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or among the goats.' Why does the פסוק need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last phrase of the פסוק and asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats were already included in the earlier law of נסכים, so the גמרא wants to know what these words come to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats

phrases.english: "Or among the goats"
why does the verse need to say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question, applied to the last phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra teaching comes from 'או בעזים'?

steps.title: Young and old goats get the same נסכים
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה separated a כבש from an איל, we might also split a young goat (גדי) from an older goat (שעיר). The phrase teaches that they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we found that the פסוק made a difference between the נסכים of a male lamb and the נסכים of a ram, maybe we should also make a difference between the נסכים of a young goat and those of an older goat? So the פסוק says 'or among the goats'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that goats of any age get the same נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats are a different kind of animal from sheep, so we might have thought they also have a young/old split like sheep do. 'או בעזים' teaches one amount for all goats. This finishes the explanation of the whole פסוק: only the male sheep has the age difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A young goat, a kid
An older goat

steps.whatToRemember: The only age difference in נסכים is between a male כבש and an איל. Bulls, female sheep and goats each get one fixed amount, no matter their age.

phrases.english: Since we found that the verse made a difference
between the libations of a male lamb and the libations of a ram,
one might think we should make a difference between the libations of a young goat
and the libations of an older goat.
Therefore the verse says: "Or among the goats."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and finishes going through the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A young goat and an older goat get the same נסכים.

steps.title: רב פפא begins: רבא tested us
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא opens a story in which רבא tested him and his friends with a question. The question itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבא tested us.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב פפא starts telling how רבא tested his students, and the actual test question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been ruled yet. The line connects to the topic just mentioned, the נסכים of female sheep, and prepares a new question from רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He tested us (checked our knowledge)
